::: {.callout-tip title="About this page" icon="false"}
A structured reference map of the Transformer era (2017 — present),
organized three ways: chronological, by architecture family, and by
application area. Each entry states the primary contribution, the key
formalization where one exists, and why it mattered. Use it as a reading
guide or as a lookup when a chapter references a work without full derivation.

Years reflect first public availability (arXiv or blog post). Citation links
point to the peer-reviewed venue, which may differ by up to one year.
:::

  </ul></td>
</tr>

    <li>No architecture change — training recipe is the difference</li>
    <li>Set a new BERT baseline; showed that pretraining details dominate architecture choice</li>
  </ul></td>
</tr>

  </ul></td>
</tr>

  <td>2019</td>
  <td><strong>BART</strong> [@lewis2019bart]<br/><small>Lewis et al. (Facebook)</small></td>
  <td><span class="tag t-ed">Enc-Dec</span></td>
  <td><ul>
    <li>Denoising pretraining: corrupt input text (masking, deletion, permutation), train encoder-decoder to reconstruct</li>
    <li>Corruption functions include token masking, text infilling, document rotation, sentence permutation</li>
    <li>SOTA on CNN/DailyMail summarisation; strong baseline for conditional generation; widely used in multilingual settings</li>
  </ul></td>
</tr>

<tr>
  <td>2020</td>
  <td><strong>Scaling laws</strong> [@kaplan2020]<br/><small>Kaplan et al. (OpenAI)</small></td>
  <td><span class="tag t-inf">Research</span></td>
  <td><ul>
    <li>Loss follows power laws in N (params), D (tokens), C (compute) independently</li>
    <li><code>L(N) ∝ N^{-α_N}</code>; optimal allocation: <code>N ∝ C^{0.73}</code></li>
    <li>Changed how every subsequent model was budgeted; predicted GPT-3 performance before training</li>
  </ul></td>
</tr>

<tr>
  <td>2020</td>
  <td><strong>GPT-3</strong> [@brown2020]<br/><small>Brown et al. (OpenAI)</small></td>
  <td><span class="tag t-do">Dec-only</span></td>
  <td><ul>
    <li>175B params; in-context few-shot learning without any weight updates</li>
    <li>Prompt: <code>[example₁] [example₂] [query] →</code> completion (no gradient)</li>
    <li>Emergence of reasoning at scale; API-as-product model; opened the LLM era</li>
  </ul></td>
</tr>

<tr>
  <td>2020</td>
  <td><strong>ViT</strong> [@dosovitskiy2021]<br/><small>Dosovitskiy et al. (Google)</small></td>
  <td><span class="tag t-eo">Enc-only</span></td>
  <td><ul>
    <li>Images split into 16×16 pixel patches; each patch linearly projected and treated as a token</li>
    <li><code>z₀ = [x_cls; x¹E; …; x^N E] + E_pos</code></li>
    <li>Proved Transformers competitive with CNNs at scale; spawned DeiT, Swin, DINO, SAM</li>
  </ul></td>
</tr>

<tr>
  <td>2021</td>
  <td><strong>Switch Transformer</strong> [@fedus2021switch]<br/><small>Fedus et al. (Google)</small></td>
  <td><span class="tag t-inf">Arch</span></td>
  <td><ul>
    <li>Simplifies MoE to top-1 routing (one expert per token); billion-to-trillion params with controlled compute</li>
    <li>Auxiliary load-balancing loss: <code>L_aux = α · Σ f_i · p_i</code></li>
    <li>Demonstrated trillion-parameter models are trainable; foundation of Mixtral and DeepSeek MoE</li>
  </ul></td>
</tr>

<tr>
  <td>2021</td>
  <td><strong>CLIP</strong> [@radford2021clip]<br/><small>Radford et al. (OpenAI)</small></td>
  <td><span class="tag t-mm">Multimodal</span></td>
  <td><ul>
    <li>Contrastive pretraining on 400M image-text pairs; separate image and text encoders</li>
    <li>Maximize <code>cos(f_I, f_T)</code> for matching pairs; InfoNCE loss</li>
    <li>Universal vision-language backbone; powers DALL-E 2, Stable Diffusion conditioning</li>
  </ul></td>
</tr>

<tr>
  <td>2021</td>
  <td><strong>AlphaFold 2</strong> [@jumper2021]<br/><small>Jumper et al. (DeepMind)</small></td>
  <td><span class="tag t-mm">Science</span></td>
  <td><ul>
    <li>Evoformer applies attention over multiple sequence alignments; geometry-aware pair representations</li>
    <li>Triangle attention: <code>a_{ij} = softmax(b_{ij} + Σ_k b_{ik} + b_{kj})</code></li>
    <li>Solved 50-year protein structure prediction problem; directly accelerated drug discovery</li>
  </ul></td>
</tr>

<tr>
  <td>2021</td>
  <td><strong>Codex</strong> [@chen2021codex]<br/><small>Chen et al. (OpenAI)</small></td>
  <td><span class="tag t-do">Dec-only</span></td>
  <td><ul>
    <li>GPT fine-tuned on 54M public GitHub repos; generates, completes, and explains code</li>
    <li>pass@k metric: probability at least 1 of k samples passes all unit tests</li>
    <li>Ships as GitHub Copilot (2022); established code as a first-class LLM domain</li>
  </ul></td>
</tr>

<tr>
  <td>2022</td>
  <td><strong>Chinchilla</strong> [@hoffmann2022]<br/><small>Hoffmann et al. (DeepMind)</small></td>
  <td><span class="tag t-inf">Research</span></td>
  <td><ul>
    <li>Kaplan exponents were wrong: params and tokens should scale equally for compute-optimal training</li>
    <li><code>N* ≈ D* ≈ (C / 6)^{0.5}</code>; GPT-3 was under-trained by ~4×</li>
    <li>Invalidated the GPT-3 era strategy; every post-2022 model (LLaMA, Gemini, Mistral) follows this</li>
  </ul></td>
</tr>

<tr>
  <td>2022</td>
  <td><strong>LoRA</strong> [@hu2022lora]<br/><small>Hu et al. (Microsoft)</small></td>
  <td><span class="tag t-inf">PEFT</span></td>
  <td><ul>
    <li>Freeze pretrained weights; inject low-rank decomposition <code>ΔW = BA</code> (rank r ≪ d)</li>
    <li><code>W' = W₀ + BA</code>, only A,B trained; reduces trainable params by 10 000×</li>
    <li>Made fine-tuning accessible on consumer hardware; used in almost every open fine-tune</li>
  </ul></td>
</tr>

<tr>
  <td>2022</td>
  <td><strong>Chain-of-Thought</strong> [@wei2022cot]<br/><small>Wei et al. (Google)</small></td>
  <td><span class="tag t-inf">Prompting</span></td>
  <td><ul>
    <li>Adding intermediate reasoning steps to few-shot examples dramatically improves multi-step reasoning</li>
    <li>Prompt: <code>"Let's think step by step..."</code> before the answer</li>
    <li>Revealed emergent reasoning in large models; direct precursor to o1 and test-time scaling</li>
  </ul></td>
</tr>

<tr>
  <td>2022</td>
  <td><strong>Flash Attention</strong> [@dao2022flashattn]<br/><small>Dao et al. (Stanford)</small></td>
  <td><span class="tag t-inf">Efficiency</span></td>
  <td><ul>
    <li>IO-aware exact attention: tile softmax computation, fuse kernels, avoid materialising O(N²) attention matrix in HBM</li>
    <li>Online softmax; recompute activations in backward pass rather than store</li>
    <li>2–4× speedup; enabled contexts beyond 8K; universally adopted from 2023 onward</li>
  </ul></td>
</tr>

<tr>
  <td>2022</td>
  <td><strong>InstructGPT</strong> [@ouyang2022]<br/><small>Ouyang et al. (OpenAI)</small></td>
  <td><span class="tag t-aln">Alignment</span></td>
  <td><ul>
    <li>RLHF pipeline: supervised fine-tuning → reward model → PPO policy optimisation</li>
    <li><code>r(x,y) − β log[π_RL(y|x) / π_SFT(y|x)]</code></li>
    <li>Direct precursor to ChatGPT; established RLHF as the default alignment method</li>
  </ul></td>
</tr>

<tr>
  <td>2022</td>
  <td><strong>Whisper</strong> [@radford2022whisper]<br/><small>Radford et al. (OpenAI)</small></td>
  <td><span class="tag t-ed">Enc-Dec</span></td>
  <td><ul>
    <li>Encoder-decoder Transformer trained on 680K hours of web audio in 96 languages</li>
    <li>Mel spectrogram encoder → text decoder; multitask via special tokens (<code>&lt;|translate|&gt;</code>, etc.)</li>
    <li>First robust open-weights ASR; standard baseline; Whisper large v3 still used in 2026</li>
  </ul></td>
</tr>

<tr>
  <td>2022</td>
  <td><strong>ChatGPT</strong><br/><small>OpenAI</small></td>
  <td><span class="tag t-do">Dec-only</span></td>
  <td><ul>
    <li>GPT-3.5 + RLHF + instruction tuning deployed as a conversational product</li>
    <li>100M users in 2 months; redefined public understanding of AI</li>
  </ul></td>
</tr>

<tr>
  <td>2023</td>
  <td><strong>QLoRA</strong> [@dettmers2023qlora]<br/><small>Dettmers et al. (UW)</small></td>
  <td><span class="tag t-inf">PEFT</span></td>
  <td><ul>
    <li>Quantise frozen base model to 4-bit NF4; inject trainable LoRA adapters; backpropagate through quantised weights</li>
    <li>NF4 format: <code>4-bit normal float</code> quantisation preserving gradient signal; paged optimisers for memory spikes</li>
    <li>Fine-tune a 65B model on a single 48 GB GPU; democratised instruction tuning; basis of Guanaco and most open fine-tunes</li>
  </ul></td>
</tr>

<tr>
  <td>2023</td>
  <td><strong>Speculative decoding</strong> [@chen2023speculative]<br/><small>Chen et al. (Google)</small></td>
  <td><span class="tag t-inf">Efficiency</span></td>
  <td><ul>
    <li>Small draft model proposes <em>k</em> tokens; target model verifies all in a single forward pass; accept or reject via sampling</li>
    <li>Acceptance criterion preserves exact target distribution: <code>p_accept = min(1, p_target / p_draft)</code></li>
    <li>2–3× inference speedup with zero quality loss; now standard in production (TGI, vLLM, TensorRT-LLM)</li>
  </ul></td>
</tr>

<tr>
  <td>2023</td>
  <td><strong>LLaMA</strong> [@touvron2023llama]<br/><small>Touvron et al. (Meta)</small></td>
  <td><span class="tag t-do">Dec-only</span></td>
  <td><ul>
    <li>Open weights with Chinchilla-optimal training; modern SLM stack: RoPE + RMSNorm + SwiGLU + GQA</li>
    <li>RoPE: <code>q_m · k_n → Re[(q_m e^{imθ})(k_n e^{inθ})^*]</code></li>
    <li>Baseline for all open-source research; spawned Alpaca, Vicuna, Mistral, Llama 2/3</li>
  </ul></td>
</tr>

<tr>
  <td>2023</td>
  <td><strong>GPT-4</strong><br/><small>OpenAI</small></td>
  <td><span class="tag t-do">Dec-only</span></td>
  <td><ul>
    <li>Multimodal (image + text input); large-scale RLHF; architecture undisclosed but widely assumed MoE</li>
    <li>Bar exam top-10%, medical licensing, coding competitions — benchmark SOTA across domains</li>
  </ul></td>
</tr>

<tr>
  <td>2023</td>
  <td><strong>DPO</strong> [@rafailov2023]<br/><small>Rafailov et al. (Stanford)</small></td>
  <td><span class="tag t-aln">Alignment</span></td>
  <td><ul>
    <li>Alignment without RL: directly optimises a closed-form loss derived from the RLHF reward</li>
    <li><code>L_DPO = −log σ[β log(π(y_w)/π_ref) − β log(π(y_l)/π_ref)]</code></li>
    <li>Simpler and more stable than PPO; default fine-tuning method for most open-source models</li>
  </ul></td>
</tr>

<tr>
  <td>2023</td>
  <td><strong>Mistral 7B</strong> [@jiang2023mistral]<br/><small>Jiang et al. (Mistral AI)</small></td>
  <td><span class="tag t-do">Dec-only</span></td>
  <td><ul>
    <li>GQA + sliding window attention; outperforms LLaMA-2 13B on most benchmarks at 7B params</li>
    <li>GQA: fewer KV heads than Q heads; sliding window: attend only to last <em>w</em> tokens per layer</li>
    <li>Demonstrated architecture efficiency matters at 7B; led to Mixtral (sparse MoE, Dec 2023)</li>
  </ul></td>
</tr>

<tr>
  <td>2023</td>
  <td><strong>Mamba</strong> [@gu2023mamba]<br/><small>Gu &amp; Dao (CMU / Stanford)</small></td>
  <td><span class="tag t-alt">Alt-Arch</span></td>
  <td><ul>
    <li>Selective state space model: input-dependent SSM parameters let the model filter or remember content selectively</li>
    <li>Hidden state: <code>h_t = A_t h_{t-1} + B_t x_t</code>; output: <code>y_t = C_t h_t</code> — A,B,C are functions of input</li>
    <li>Linear-time inference; matches Transformer quality at language modelling; opened serious competition to quadratic attention</li>
  </ul></td>
</tr>

<tr>
  <td>2023</td>
  <td><strong>Gemini</strong> [@team2023gemini]<br/><small>Google DeepMind</small></td>
  <td><span class="tag t-mm">Multimodal</span></td>
  <td><ul>
    <li>Natively multimodal decoder (text, image, audio, video, code); three sizes (Ultra, Pro, Nano); MoE-based</li>
    <li>Trained on interleaved multimodal sequences end-to-end rather than late-fusion of separate encoders</li>
    <li>First model to match or exceed GPT-4 on key benchmarks at release; Gemini 1.5 introduced 1M-token context window</li>
  </ul></td>
</tr>

<tr>
  <td>2024</td>
  <td><strong>o1</strong><br/><small>OpenAI</small></td>
  <td><span class="tag t-do">Dec-only</span></td>
  <td><ul>
    <li>Test-time compute scaling: extended chain-of-thought as inference, not training</li>
    <li>RL on verifiable reasoning tasks; more inference tokens → better answers</li>
    <li>Opened a second scaling axis (inference FLOPs); reasoning model paradigm now widespread</li>
  </ul></td>
</tr>

<tr>
  <td>2024</td>
  <td><strong>Sora</strong><br/><small>OpenAI</small></td>
  <td><span class="tag t-mm">Video</span></td>
  <td><ul>
    <li>Diffusion Transformer (DiT): patches spacetime video into tokens; Transformer denoising backbone replaces UNet</li>
    <li>Unified representation of images, video, audio as sequences of spacetime patches at variable resolution and length</li>
    <li>First model to generate coherent minute-long videos with object permanence; "GPT-1 moment" for video generation</li>
  </ul></td>
</tr>

<tr>
  <td>2024</td>
  <td><strong>DeepSeek-V2 / MLA</strong> [@deepseekv2team2024]<br/><small>DeepSeek AI</small></td>
  <td><span class="tag t-inf">Efficiency</span></td>
  <td><ul>
    <li>Multi-head Latent Attention (MLA): compress K,V into a low-rank latent vector <code>c_t^{KV}</code>, reconstruct via up-projection at inference</li>
    <li><code>KV cache per token: d_c ≪ n_h × d_h</code> (e.g., 5× compression vs standard MHA)</li>
    <li>Reduces KV cache by up to 93%; enables longer context at lower memory cost; adopted in DeepSeek-V3/R1</li>
  </ul></td>
</tr>

<tr>
  <td>2025</td>
  <td><strong>DeepSeek-R1</strong><br/><small>DeepSeek AI</small></td>
  <td><span class="tag t-do">Dec-only</span></td>
  <td><ul>
    <li>Open reasoning model trained with RL only (GRPO — no value model); 671B sparse MoE</li>
    <li>GRPO: group relative policy optimisation using outcome rewards only</li>
    <li>o1-level reasoning at ~1/30 cost; largest open-weights frontier model as of early 2026</li>
  </ul></td>
</tr>

</tbody>
</table>

## By architecture family

### Encoder-Decoder {.unnumbered}

Two stacks: encoder reads the full source bidirectionally; decoder generates
target tokens autoregressively with cross-attention to all encoder states.
The original Transformer family, and still dominant for structured generation
(MT, summarisation, speech).

| Work | Year | Key specialisation |
|---|---|---|
| Transformer [@vaswani2017] | 2017 | Machine translation; established the architecture |
| T5 [@raffel2020] | 2019 | Text-to-text unification; systematic scaling study |
| BART (Lewis et al., 2019) | 2019 | Denoising pretraining; strong summarisation |
| Whisper [@radford2022whisper] | 2022 | Multilingual speech; weak-supervision at scale |
| mT5 (Xue et al., 2021) | 2021 | Multilingual T5 across 101 languages |

Encoder-decoder peaked around 2020–2022. Decoder-only models at sufficient
scale can perform the same tasks, reducing incentive to maintain the split.

### Encoder-only {.unnumbered}

A bidirectional Transformer pretrained on a self-supervised objective;
fine-tuned representations for downstream tasks. Strong for classification,
extraction, and retrieval; cannot generate fluently.

| Work | Year | Objective | Key strength |
|---|---|---|---|
| BERT [@devlin2019] | 2018 | MLM + NSP | Bidirectional; defined fine-tuning paradigm |
| RoBERTa [@liu2019roberta] | 2019 | MLM only | Better training recipe; new BERT baseline |
| ViT [@dosovitskiy2021] | 2020 | Patch classification | Transformers for vision |
| CLIP [@radford2021clip] | 2021 | Contrastive image-text | Universal multimodal backbone |
| DeBERTa (He et al., 2021) | 2021 | MLM + disentangled attn | Disentangled position representations |

Now used primarily for embeddings, retrieval (dense passage retrieval,
bi-encoders), and cross-modal alignment rather than generation.

### Decoder-only {.unnumbered}

A causal (left-to-right) Transformer pretrained as a language model.
By 2022 this family dominates every benchmark and every major product.

| Work | Year | Scale | Key advance |
|---|---|---|---|
| GPT-1 [@radford2018gpt] | 2018 | 117M | Pretraining + fine-tuning paradigm |
| GPT-2 [@radford2019gpt2] | 2019 | 1.5B | Zero-shot task transfer |
| GPT-3 [@brown2020] | 2020 | 175B | In-context few-shot learning; emergence |
| Codex [@chen2021codex] | 2021 | 12B | Code generation; GitHub Copilot |
| InstructGPT [@ouyang2022] | 2022 | 175B | RLHF alignment |
| LLaMA [@touvron2023llama] | 2023 | 7–65B | Open weights; modern SLM architecture stack |
| GPT-4 | 2023 | undisclosed | Multimodal; SOTA across all benchmarks |
| o1 | 2024 | undisclosed | Test-time compute scaling |
| DeepSeek-R1 | 2025 | 671B (MoE) | Open frontier reasoning model |

### Mixture of Experts (MoE) {.unnumbered}

A routing mechanism layered on top of any Transformer: each token activates
only a subset of FFN experts, keeping active compute constant while total
parameters grow.

| Work | Year | Routing | Notable use |
|---|---|---|---|
| Sparse MoE [@shazeer2017moe] | 2017 | Top-k soft gate | Founding paper; 137B params |
| Switch Transformer [@fedus2021switch] | 2021 | Top-1 hard | Trillion-param training |
| Mixtral 8×7B (Jiang et al., 2024) | 2024 | Top-2 of 8 | First competitive open MoE |
| DeepSeek-V3 (2024) | 2024 | Top-2 of 256 | 671B sparse; frontier quality at open cost |

MoE is the dominant architecture at frontier scale. GPT-4, Gemini 1.5, and
almost every post-2023 flagship model is believed to use sparse MoE.

### Methods: training, alignment, efficiency {.unnumbered}

Works that changed how models are trained, aligned, or deployed without
introducing a new architecture family.

| Work | Year | Type | Core contribution |
|---|---|---|---|
| Scaling laws [@kaplan2020] | 2020 | Training | Power-law training budgets |
| Chinchilla [@hoffmann2022] | 2022 | Training | Optimal token/param ratio; equal scaling |
| LoRA [@hu2022lora] | 2022 | PEFT | Low-rank weight injection; 10 000× fewer trainable params |
| Chain-of-Thought [@wei2022cot] | 2022 | Prompting | Intermediate reasoning steps unlock multi-step tasks |
| Flash Attention [@dao2022flashattn] | 2022 | Efficiency | IO-aware exact attention; 2–4× speedup |
| InstructGPT RLHF [@ouyang2022] | 2022 | Alignment | PPO from human preferences |
| DPO [@rafailov2023] | 2023 | Alignment | Closed-form preference loss; replaces PPO |
| RAG [@lewis2020rag] | 2020 | Retrieval | Non-parametric memory: retrieve passages, condition generation on them |
| RoPE [@su2024rope] | 2021 | PE | Rotary position encoding; adopted by LLaMA family |
| MQA (Shazeer, 2019) | 2019 | Efficiency | Multi-query attention: all Q heads share one K,V head |
| GQA [@ainslie2023gqa] | 2023 | Efficiency | Grouped-query: G shared KV groups; interpolates MHA↔MQA |
| MLA [@deepseekv2team2024] | 2024 | Efficiency | Low-rank KV compression; up to 93% KV cache reduction |
| QLoRA [@dettmers2023qlora] | 2023 | PEFT | 4-bit NF4 quantisation + LoRA adapters; single-GPU fine-tuning |
| Speculative decoding [@chen2023speculative] | 2023 | Efficiency | Draft-verify pipeline; 2–3× throughput, exact distribution |

### Alternative architectures: beyond quadratic attention {.unnumbered}

The Transformer's $O(N^2)$ attention cost motivates research into sub-linear
alternatives. None has displaced Transformers at scale, but Mamba and hybrids
are serious contenders for 2025–2026.

| Work | Year | Mechanism | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| Mamba [@gu2023mamba] | 2023 | Selective SSM — input-dependent state transitions | Competitive at small scale; Mamba-2 unifies SSM ↔ attention |
| RWKV (Peng et al., 2023) | 2023 | Linear attention via token-shift recurrence | LLM-scale open model (14B); constant inference memory |
| RetNet (Sun et al., 2023) | 2023 | Retention: parallel train, sequential infer | "Training Parallelism + Inference Efficiency + Performance" triangle |
| Griffin (DeepMind, 2024) | 2024 | Gated linear recurrence + local attention hybrid | Matches Llama at 14B; inference-efficient |

The most likely outcome is **hybrid architectures** that mix attention layers (for long-range global context) with SSM or linear recurrence layers (for local computation efficiency).

::: {.callout-note title="Out of scope: Graph Neural Networks" icon="false"}
**Graph Neural Networks** (GCN, GAT, and successors) address a different
input structure, arbitrary graphs rather than sequences or grids, and are
deliberately out of scope for this timeline. They are omitted by design,
not by oversight: this book traces the sequence-and-grid lineage (RNN → CNN
→ Transformer) rather than the parallel graph-representation-learning
lineage.
:::

## By application area

| Domain | Landmark work | Available | Current state |
|---|---|---|---|
| Machine translation | Transformer 2017 | 2017 | Transformer MT is the industry standard |
| NLU / QA / classification | BERT 2018 | 2019 | Fine-tuned encoders or few-shot LLMs |
| Text generation | GPT-2 2019 | 2019 | GPT-4o, Claude 4, Gemini 2.x, LLaMA 3 |
| Code generation | Codex 2021 | 2022 (Copilot) | Claude, DeepSeek-Coder, GPT-4o |
| Image classification | ViT 2020 | 2021 | ViT, DeiT, Swin, DINO v2 |
| Image generation | CLIP + diffusion 2021 | 2022 | Stable Diffusion, DALL-E 3, Flux, Midjourney |
| Video generation | Sora (DiT) 2024 | 2024 | Sora 2, Veo 2, Kling, Wan |
| Speech recognition | Whisper 2022 | 2022 | Whisper v3, Distil-Whisper |
| Protein structure | AlphaFold 2 [@jumper2021] 2021 | 2021 | AlphaFold 3, ESMFold, ESM3 |
| Reasoning | CoT [@wei2022cot] + o1 2024 | 2024 | o3, DeepSeek-R1, Gemini Thinking |
| Agents and tool use | GPT-4 function calls 2023 | 2023 | Multi-agent frameworks, Claude tool use |
| Long-context understanding | Flash Attn + LLaMA 2023 | 2023 | 1M+ context windows (Gemini 1.5 Pro) |
| Efficient fine-tuning | LoRA 2022 | 2022 | QLoRA, DoRA, widely used open-source |
